decisions.reason: Correctly traces resolve() in plugin/src-client-index.ts: sessions.list.getSnapshot() succeeds but the alpha.2 snapshot payload has no current field, so id is undefined, resolve() returns null, and onKeyDown exits before preventDefault. Explains both silences: all four guard presence probes survive because only a field inside the published value was removed, and undefined was a legitimate no-session state the code deliberately ignores. Correctly notes the services were not removed or renamed and nothing throws, and identifies which already-tried items are settled versus untouched.

Grounded diff of the two session-controller excerpts: SessionListState.current is gone and navigation moved to view owners per the ISessions.list doc comment; the replacement is the uiSession service's adapter.current ObservableSnapshot<SessionBindingValue> yielding { key, ctx, hooks, keyedHooks, props }, with key replacing current and ctx explicitly identified as replacing sessions.scope(id). Full type-walk from the sealed excerpts.

Provides concrete fenced code reading uiSession.adapter.current.getSnapshot() when the service exists and falling back to legacy current plus sessions.scope otherwise, from one build; inject gains uiSession while keeping sessions; the conversation service resolves through binding ctx via ctx.get('conversation') and input.for receives that session-scoped ctx. Branch selection by service presence, not version string.

Names the breakage class as field-level removal behind surviving service members, probed once at activation while the break recurs per use. Hardened guard probes the actual snapshot shape (assert current on alpha-1-shaped hosts, feature-detect uiSession and its key/ctx on alpha-2-shaped hosts), exercises the functional read, and explicitly requires the probe to run lazily/per-use (first binding emission and session switch), not only at activation. Not mere presence-list expansion.

Verification covers a live DevTools probe of adapter.current/ctx with a session open, chord behavior after the code change on both hosts via side-by-side install, and unit tests against literal snapshot shapes; prevention gives a throwing deprecated getter or runtime fail-loud alternative. However, the report never proposes typechecking the plugin against alpha.2's published types as the strongest pre-ship gate, one of the criterion's required verification elements.

caps.reason: The final remedy is the corrected dual-host resolution code plus inject addition; the report explicitly states merely re-declaring inject or re-registering slots would not restore recall because the old read path still reads a removed field. The colleague's red herring is quoted and rejected, not endorsed.
